cards.text: Remember Stephen, the believer they stoned for his faith (Acts 7:59)? A persecution began with him, and the believers scattered as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus and Antioch. And everywhere they go, they're sharing the message.

cards.question: At first, the scattered believers speak the message only to ___.

cards.text: But some of them, men from Cyprus and Cyrene, get to Antioch and open the door WIDE. They're the one coworker who invites the whole building to the party, not just his department.

cards.question: In Antioch, what do the men from Cyprus and Cyrene start doing?

answers.text: Telling the Greeks about Jesus too
Telling the Romans about Jesus too
Telling the Egyptians about Jesus too

cards.text: We never even get these guys' names, and I had mine CARVED into my handle and still ended up in a junk drawer. Doesn't matter, because the hand of the Lord is with them.

cards.question: Only a handful of people in Antioch believe and turn to the Lord.

cards.text: A GREAT number. That's not a small group anymore, that's a stadium, and the news reaches the ears of the church in Jerusalem.

cards.question: When the church in Jerusalem hears what's happening, they send ___ to Antioch.

cards.text: Barnabas is a believer from Cyprus who once sold a field and brought the money to the apostles (Acts 4:36-37). He arrives in Antioch, looks around, and sees the grace of God.

cards.question: When Barnabas sees the grace of God in Antioch, he's troubled by it.

cards.text: He rejoices, and he encourages them all to abide in the Lord with all their hearts. His name means Son of Encouragement (Acts 4:36), so the man is out here LIVING his name tag.

cards.question: Acts sums Barnabas up in just a few words. Which description fits him?

answers.text: A good man full of the Holy Spirit and faith
A bold man full of zeal and power
A wise man full of learning and grace

cards.question: With Barnabas there in Antioch, a great number of people are brought to the Lord.

cards.text: Then Barnabas heads to Tarsus to look for somebody. No phone, no GPS, just a whole city and one name, and that's COMMITMENT, friend.

cards.question: Who is Barnabas looking for in Tarsus?

cards.text: Saul is the man who once breathed threats against believers until Jesus stopped him on the road to Damascus (Acts 9:1-6). Barnabas finds him and brings him back to Antioch.

cards.question: Barnabas and Saul stay in Antioch only a few days before moving on.

cards.text: A full YEAR meeting with the church and teaching large numbers of people. The only thing I ever stuck with for a whole year was the junk drawer, and nobody asked me.

cards.question: In Antioch, the disciples get a name for the very first time. They're called ___.

cards.text: In those days, some prophets come down from Jerusalem to Antioch. One of them, Agabus, stands up and predicts through the Spirit what's coming, and it's not good news.

cards.question: What does Agabus predict will sweep across the whole world?

cards.text: And it really happens, under Claudius, the Roman emperor. Most folks hear news like that and start hiding cookies in the back of the cupboard, but watch these disciples.

cards.question: The disciples in Antioch decide to send relief to the brothers living in ___.
The disciples in Antioch all agree to give the exact same amount.
Who carries the Antioch disciples' gifts to the elders?

cards.text: Each disciple gives according to his ability, and Barnabas and Saul carry it all to the elders. A church started by guys we don't even have names for is now sending help to Judea, and I'm getting choked up over here.

findings.problem: "The believer they stoned for his faith" gives a reason the text doesn't state. Acts 7:54-58 shows the crowd's rage at Stephen's words and his vision, but it never says they stoned him "for his faith." Saying simply that he was stoned (Acts 7:59) would keep to the text.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The baker has to pick the exact wording Acts uses for Barnabas. Nothing on the earlier cards helps them tell "a good man full of the Holy Spirit and faith" from "a bold man full of zeal and power" or "a wise man full of learning and grace." Card 11 shows him encouraging people, which fits all three. It's a guess at wording, not a reasoned pick.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: "The only thing I ever stuck with for a whole year was the junk drawer" contradicts the backstory. Papa Dorin spent years on the Millers' counter and was part of every batch. The joke changes his story.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: "The disciples get a name for the very first time" stretches Acts 11:26. The text says they were first called Christians at Antioch, not that they had no name before. Acts 9:2 calls them those who belonged to the Way. The question should say they were first called ___ at Antioch.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: This closing story card retells what the baker just answered on cards 11 and 12: each giving according to ability, and Barnabas and Saul carrying the gift to the elders. It moves nothing forward, so it works as a recap card.

"A church started by guys we don't even have names for" says more than the text. Acts 11:19-20 shows the scattered believers reaching Antioch first, speaking to Jews, and then the men from Cyprus and Cyrene speaking to the Greeks as well. The text never says those men started the church in Antioch.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
